apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: deploy-host
  title: System deployment manifests (shared)
  description: The Dapr components a system's blocks share, as one ArgoCD Application.
  tags: [deploy, gitops, kustomize, dapr]
  labels:
    intropy.dev/template-kind: deploy
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    # domain is optional, deliberately: it is only a GitOps path segment, no
    # skeleton references it outside component.yaml (repo metadata a local render
    # never emits), and a local render has no domain.
    required: [system, namespace]
    properties:
      domain:
        type: string
        title: Domain
        description: Business domain the system belongs to, as a GitOps path segment. Not required — a local render has no domain, and no skeleton references it outside component.yaml, which local rendering never emits.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      system:
        type: string
        title: System
        description: System name, as a GitOps path segment.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespace:
        type: string
        title: Namespace
        description: The Kubernetes namespace the system's blocks run in. With namespacePerEnv the environment is prefixed to it.
        default: integrations
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespacePerEnv:
        type: boolean
        title: Namespace per environment
        description: Prefix the environment to the namespace, e.g. test-acme-integrations. Leave false for a single flat namespace.
        default: false
      pubsub:
        type: string
        title: Pub/sub broker
        description: The Dapr pub/sub building block to declare, from deploy.yaml platform.pubsub. rabbitmq is what local rendering uses.
        enum: [in-memory, rabbitmq, servicebus]
        default: rabbitmq
      pubsubName:
        type: string
        title: Pub/sub component name
        description: The name blocks resolve the broker by. Must match what the generated C# uses.
        default: pubsub
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
  values:
    secretName: "{{ .system }}-secrets"

  # Which files exist at all, rather than only what is in them. First match
  # decides; a path no rule matches is always included.
  files:
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-in-memory.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "in-memory" }}'
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-rabbitmq.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "rabbitmq" }}'
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-servicebus.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "servicebus" }}'

    # The generic environment overlay never renders for the local environment:
    # it would set a namespace line, while the local overlay stays
    # namespace-agnostic (local rendering sets the namespace on the root
    # kustomization it writes). A dedicated overlays/local/ skeleton carries
    # that thin-but-namespaceless variant. local is reserved — no customer
    # environment may be named that.
    - path: 'overlays/{{ .env }}/**'
      when: '{{ ne .env "local" }}'

    # No external connectors means no bindings, and an empty multi-doc file in a
    # kustomize resources list breaks the build. Never for the local environment:
    # the fixture catalog on deploy-component carries the local bindings, and a
    # REPLACE-ME scaffold here would duplicate every Component the fixtures
    # render.
    - path: base/bindings/**
      when: '{{ and (gt (len .topology.connectors) 0) (ne .env "local") }}'

apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: deploy-component
  title: Block deployment manifests
  description: The workload and overlays for one block, as one ArgoCD Application.
  tags: [deploy, gitops, kustomize]
  labels:
    intropy.dev/template-kind: deploy
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    # domain is optional, deliberately: it is only a GitOps path segment, no
    # skeleton references it, and a local render has no domain. GitOps creation
    # derives it from the destination or requires --domain.
    required: [name, system, registry]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Component
        description: Block name, as a GitOps path segment.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      domain:
        type: string
        title: Domain
        description: Only a GitOps path segment; no skeleton file references it.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      system:
        type: string
        title: System
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      appId:
        type: string
        title: Dapr app-id
        description: The identity the sidecar registers as, and what a Component's scopes list.
      kind:
        type: string
        title: Block kind
        description: The topology's block kind, carried through as a label.
        default: ""
      workload:
        type: string
        title: Workload
        description: An extractor is scheduled and exits; everything else stays resident.
        enum: [cronjob, deployment]
        default: deployment
      namespace:
        type: string
        title: Namespace
        default: integrations
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespacePerEnv:
        type: boolean
        title: Namespace per environment
        default: false
      registry:
        type: string
        title: Registry
        description: The registry from deploy.yaml.
      imageNamespace:
        type: string
        title: Image namespace
        description: The path segment between the registry and the image name. Must match what CI pushes.
        default: integrations
      replicas:
        type: integer
        title: Replicas
        default: 1
      sourceDir:
        type: string
        title: Source directory
        description: The block's directory in the source repository, used for component.yaml sourcePaths. Empty when no scaffold record was found.
        default: ""
  # The closed fixture catalog for the local development cluster: one Dapr
  # binding skeleton per fixture type in overlays/local/fixtures/, switched on
  # the connector's binding for this render. Local manifest rendering fails a
  # release that ships a local overlay without this list and validates explicit
  # or interactive choices against it. Adding a fixture is a skeleton file, an
  # entry here, and the fixture server in the k3s setup scripts — a template PR,
  # not a CLI release.
  local:
    fixtures: [sftp, smb, http, file]

  values:
    imageRepo: "{{ .registry }}/{{ .imageNamespace }}/{{ .name }}"
    # Never a real tag. `intropy deploy pin` writes the digest; a tag here would let
    # what runs change without a deployment, which is the whole thing this
    # toolchain exists to prevent.
    imageTag: "unpinned"

  files:
    # The CronJob's schedule is deployment configuration that differs between
    # the local cluster (a dev cadence, applied unreviewed) and every other
    # environment (a REPLACE-ME a human fills in), and .env may only vary
    # under overlays/ — so the variant is picked here, per file, and
    # base/kustomization.yaml names the picked file. First match decides.
    - path: base/cronjob.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ and (eq .workload "cronjob") (ne .env "local") }}'
    - path: base/cronjob-local.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ and (eq .workload "cronjob") (eq .env "local") }}'
    - path: base/deployment.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .workload "deployment" }}'

    # The generic environment overlay never renders for the local environment:
    # it and overlays/local/ would both land at overlays/local/, and the walk
    # order ("local" sorts before "{{ .env }}") means the thin overlay would
    # silently overwrite the fixture-carrying one. local is reserved for the
    # local overlay — no customer environment may be named that.
    - path: 'overlays/{{ .env }}/**'
      when: '{{ ne .env "local" }}'

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# The local overlay. Unlike the environment overlays it carries the fixture
# bindings: every connector's Dapr binding lives next to the component that
# uses it, switched on the ephemeral choice for this render
# (spec.local.fixtures declares the catalog). It has no namespace line and no
# image override on purpose — intropy manifests render sets both on the root
# kustomization
# it writes: namespace: targets every rendered resource at once, and images[]
# rewrites the bare image reference the base renders ({{ .name }}, no registry
# prefix or tag; pinned in the README) to <name>:dev.
resources:
  - ../../base
  - fixtures/sftp.yaml
  - fixtures/smb.yaml
  - fixtures/http.yaml
  - fixtures/file.yaml
=== deploy-component/skeleton/overlays/local/fixtures/sftp.yaml.tmpl ===
# The sftp fixture: one Dapr binding per connector bound to `sftp` for the
# local environment, pointing at the SFTP server the k3s setup scripts always
# install. Address and credentials are the fixture contract (see
# deploy-component/README.md) — dev values, not placeholders.
#
# The binding travels on the connector itself: manifest rendering injects the
# explicit or interactive choice for this run. The $recorded fallback keeps a
# CLI older than that field working with the flat bindings map under .local.
#
# Owner, not user: this overlay renders once per component, and a
# connector's Component may exist exactly once in the build, so the component
# whose app-id is first in the connector's scopes emits it — scopes still
# list every app-id that may use it.
{{- $recorded := dig "local" "bindings" dict . -}}
{{- range .topology.connectors }}
{{- $conn := . }}
{{- $b := dig "binding" "" . -}}
{{- if and (or (eq $b "sftp") (and (not $b) (eq (index $recorded .name) "sftp"))) (eq $.component.appId (index $conn.appIds 0)) }}
---
apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}
  labels:
    intropy.io/connector: {{ .name }}
spec:
  type: bindings.sftp
  version: v1
  metadata:
    - name: address
      value: sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22
    - name: username
      value: intropy
    - name: password
      value: intropy
scopes:
{{- range $conn.appIds }}
  - {{ . }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
=== deploy-component/skeleton/base/deployment.yaml.tmpl ===
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}
spec:
  replicas: {{ .replicas }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: {{ .name }}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: {{ .name }}
      annotations:
        dapr.io/enabled: "true"
        dapr.io/app-id: {{ .appId }}
        dapr.io/app-port: "8080"
        dapr.io/enable-api-logging: "false"
    spec:

        - name: {{ .name }}
{{- if eq .env "local" }}
          # The pinned local reference: the bare component name, no registry
          # prefix, no tag. intropy manifests render rewrites it to <name>:dev —
          # the image the k3s scripts build and load — through the images[] entries on

          # fixture contract; only a local render may use it (manifest

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

# The local overlay, rendered by intropy manifests render --env local. Same
# resources as every other environment, but no namespace line: the CLI writes
# a root kustomization whose namespace: targets every rendered resource at once, so
# this overlay serves any --namespace without re-rendering. The generic
# overlays/{{ .env }}/ skeleton never renders for local (spec.files).
resources:
  - ../../base
=== deploy-host/skeleton/base/dapr/pubsub-rabbitmq.yaml.tmpl ===
{{- if eq .env "local" }}
# RabbitMQ pub/sub: what the local development cluster's k3s setup installs,
# and the only broker a local render ever uses. The address is the fixture
# contract (see deploy-host/README.md); the credentials are the contract's
# conventional dev credentials, inline rather than behind a Secret, because
# there is nothing to keep secret locally.
{{- end }}
apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .pubsubName }}
spec:
  type: pubsub.rabbitmq
  version: v1
  metadata:
    - name: connectionString
{{- if eq .env "local" }}
      value: REDACTED
{{- else }}
      # With no auth block, secretKeyRef resolves against a plain Kubernetes
      # Secret in this namespace. That Secret is platform-owned (synced from
      # Key Vault, Vault, or applied by hand) — the template only declares the
      # name and key the platform must provide.
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ .secretName }}
        key: rabbitmq-connection
{{- end }}
    - name: durable
      value: "true"
    - name: deliveryMode
      value: "2"
# Exactly the app-ids the topology says publish to or subscribe from this
# broker's topics. The Component is namespace-scoped and this directory is its
# only owner, so scopes is what limits who may use it.
scopes:
{{- range .topology.pubsubs }}
{{- range .appIds }}
  - {{ . }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
=== deploy-host/skeleton/base/bindings/bindings.yaml.tmpl ===
# One Dapr binding per connector the topology declares, as a multi-document file.
#
# Multi-doc rather than a file each: kustomize reads it natively, and adding a
# connector stays a one-file diff. The topology mints only the connector's name
# and scopes. Binding type, address, and credentials are environment-owned
# GitOps configuration, so create-only onboarding leaves explicit placeholders
# for the reviewer. The name must not change: blocks resolve the binding as
# binding.<connector-name>.
{{- range .topology.connectors }}
---
apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}
spec:
  # Pick the Dapr binding this connector deploys as (for example,
  # bindings.sftp or bindings.http) and fill in its metadata below.
  type: REPLACE-ME-BINDING-TYPE
  version: v1
  metadata:
    - name: REPLACE-ME-METADATA-NAME
      value: REPLACE-ME-METADATA-VALUE
scopes:
{{- range .appIds }}
  - {{ . }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

# intropy-dev-env

Curated ephemeral dev environment for Intropy tooling services
(idempotency-service, business-incident-service) on a local k3d cluster.

Everything is disposable: `./down.sh` deletes the cluster and every byte
of state with it.

## Prerequisites

- Docker Desktop (running)
- `k3d`, `kubectl`, `helm`, `dapr` CLI (`brew install k3d kubectl helm dapr/tap/dapr-cli`)
- The service repos checked out as siblings of this repo:
  - `../idempotency-service`
  - `../business-incident-service`

## Usage

```bash
./up.sh       # create cluster, install Dapr + RabbitMQ, build images, install services
./status.sh   # pods and helm releases at a glance
./down.sh     # delete the cluster; nothing persists
```

`up.sh` is idempotent — re-run it after fixing a failure and it converges.

## What gets installed

| Component | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| k3d cluster `intropy` | Docker | single-node, config in `clusters/k3d.yaml` |

- `infra/rabbitmq.yaml` and the `postgresql.image` blocks in

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# up.sh — spin up the curated ephemeral dev environment.
#
# Order matters (learned the hard way):
#   k3d cluster -> Dapr -> RabbitMQ (wait ready) -> images -> services.
# The business-incident-service daprd sidecar crash-loops if RabbitMQ
# is not accepting connections when it starts; it self-heals via restarts,
# but we wait properly so the env comes up clean.
#
# Idempotent: safe to re-run after failures; each step converges.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLUSTER_NAME="${CLUSTER_NAME:-intropy}"

# Service repo checkouts are expected as siblings of this repo.
TOOLING_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
IDEMPOTENCY_REPO="${IDEMPOTENCY_REPO:-$TOOLING_DIR/idempotency-service}"
INCIDENT_REPO="${INCIDENT_REPO:-$TOOLING_DIR/business-incident-service}"

# Branches to check for charts/images. Override to test other branches.
IDEMPOTENCY_REF="${IDEMPOTENCY_REF:-feat/ephemeral-postgres-values}"
INCIDENT_REF="${INCIDENT_REF:-feat/ephemeral-postgres-values}"

IDEM_IMAGE="local/idempotency-service:0.1.0"
BIS_IMAGE="local/business-incident-service:1.0.8"
BIS_MIGRATE_IMAGE="local/business-incident-service-migrate:1.0.8"

# Garage upstream tag to clone for its helm chart. See infra/garage.yaml for
# why we clone instead of pulling from a chart repo. appVersion of chart
# 0.9.3 matches Garage v2.3.0.
GARAGE_REF="${GARAGE_REF:-v2.3.0}"

# Pinned Garage dev credentials. NOT A SECRET — pod-ephemeral, intentionally
# fake, documented in AGENTS.md (rule #1). They must be static so SFTPGo's
# seeded user, the Dapr S3 binding (infra/dapr-s3-binding.yaml), and the
# integration repos' seed.sh can all reference them without runtime lookup.
# Format constraints come from Garage's Key::import (id >= 8 chars
# [a-zA-Z0-9._-], secret >= 16 graphic ASCII).
GARAGE_KEY_ID="GKdev0fixture0000000001"
GARAGE_KEY_SECRET="dev-fixture-secret-not-real-0001"
# Single fixtures bucket; integrations are namespaced under the sftp/ and
# blob/ roots. SFTPGo is chrooted to sftp/ (infra/sftpgo.yaml).
GARAGE_BUCKET="dev-fixtures"

NAMESPACE_INFRA="fixtures"
NAMESPACE_SERVICES="tooling"

log() { printf '\n\033[1;34m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf '\033[1;31mERROR: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Preflight
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Preflight checks"

for cmd in docker kubectl helm dapr k3d git; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "'$cmd' not found. See README prerequisites."
done

docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker is not running."

[ -d "$IDEMPOTENCY_REPO" ] || die "idempotency-service repo not found at $IDEMPOTENCY_REPO (set IDEMPOTENCY_REPO)"
[ -d "$INCIDENT_REPO" ] || die "business-incident-service repo not found at $INCIDENT_REPO (set INCIDENT_REPO)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. k3d cluster
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if k3d cluster list | grep -q "^$CLUSTER_NAME "; then
  log "k3d cluster '$CLUSTER_NAME' already exists — reusing"
else
  log "Creating k3d cluster '$CLUSTER_NAME'"
  k3d cluster create "$CLUSTER_NAME" --config clusters/k3d.yaml
fi

kubectl config use-context "k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME" >/dev/null
CONTEXT="$(kubectl config current-context)"
[ "$CONTEXT" = "k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME" ] || die "kubectl context is '$CONTEXT', expected 'k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME'. Refusing to continue."

kubectl wait --for=condition=ready node --all --timeout=120s >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Dapr
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if kubectl get namespace dapr-system >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "Dapr already installed — skipping"
else
  log "Installing Dapr"
  dapr init -k --wait
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. RabbitMQ
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Installing RabbitMQ (namespace: $NAMESPACE_INFRA)"

helm upgrade --install rabbitmq oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/rabbitmq \
  -f infra/rabbitmq.yaml \
  --namespace "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" --create-namespace

log "Waiting for RabbitMQ to accept connections"

# The StatefulSet's pod is not guaranteed to exist the moment helm returns;
# poll for existence before waiting on readiness.
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" get pod rabbitmq-0 >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 2
done
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" get pod rabbitmq-0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "rabbitmq-0 never appeared"

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" wait --for=condition=ready pod/rabbitmq-0 --timeout=300s

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3b. Garage (S3-compatible object storage)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Installing Garage (ref: $GARAGE_REF, namespace: $NAMESPACE_INFRA)"

# Upstream ships the chart only in its git repo (script/helm/garage), so we
# shallow-clone at a pinned tag into a temp dir and install from there.
GARAGE_CHART_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$GARAGE_CHART_DIR"' EXIT
git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "$GARAGE_REF" \
  https://git.deuxfleurs.fr/Deuxfleurs/garage "$GARAGE_CHART_DIR/garage" \
  || die "failed to clone garage at $GARAGE_REF"

helm upgrade --install garage "$GARAGE_CHART_DIR/garage/script/helm/garage" \
  -f infra/garage.yaml \
  --namespace "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" --create-namespace

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" rollout status statefulset/garage --timeout=300s

log "Configuring Garage cluster layout and fixtures bucket"

# Garage requires an explicit cluster layout before it stores anything, and
# layout changes are not idempotent — a second `layout assign` for the same
# node fails. Gate on the node having a configured zone/role instead.
GARAGE_POD=garage-0
garage_cli() { kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" exec "$GARAGE_POD" -- /garage "$@"; }

NODE_ID="$(garage_cli status | awk '/^ID[[:space:]]/ { in_hdr=1; next } in_hdr && NF { print $1; exit }')"
[ -n "$NODE_ID" ] || die "could not determine garage node ID"

if garage_cli status | grep -q "NO ROLE ASSIGNED"; then
  garage_cli layout assign -z dc1 -c 1G "$NODE_ID"
  garage_cli layout apply --version 1
else
  echo "Garage layout already configured — skipping"
fi

# Dev bucket + deterministic key. `key import` errors with "Key already
# exists" on re-run; filter that specific case so other errors still fail the
# script. Import (over the RPC proxy) needs no admin_token in garage.toml.
# Bucket create errors with BucketAlreadyExists on re-run; filter that case
# (like key import below) so re-runs are quiet but real errors still fail.
bucket_out="$(garage_cli bucket create "$GARAGE_BUCKET" 2>&1)" || {
  grep -qi "already exists" <<<"$bucket_out" || { echo "$bucket_out" >&2; die "garage bucket create failed"; }
}
key_out="$(garage_cli key import -n dev-key --yes "$GARAGE_KEY_ID" "$GARAGE_KEY_SECRET" 2>&1)" || {
  grep -qi "already exists" <<<"$key_out" || { echo "$key_out" >&2; die "garage key import failed"; }
}

# Grant on the pinned key ID each run: allows are idempotent and re-applying
# keeps the binding intact even if the key was recreated outside up.sh.
garage_cli bucket allow --read --write --owner "$GARAGE_BUCKET" --key "$GARAGE_KEY_ID"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3c. SFTPGo (dev SFTP fixture)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Installing SFTPGo (namespace: $NAMESPACE_INFRA)"

helm upgrade --install sftpgo oci://ghcr.io/sftpgo/helm-charts/sftpgo \
  --version 0.47.0 \
  -f infra/sftpgo.yaml \
  --namespace "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" --create-namespace

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_INFRA" rollout status deploy/sftpgo --timeout=300s

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Build and import service images
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Building and importing images"

images/build.sh "$IDEMPOTENCY_REPO" "$INCIDENT_REPO" "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
  "$IDEM_IMAGE" "$BIS_IMAGE" "$BIS_MIGRATE_IMAGE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Services
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Installing idempotency-service (ref: $IDEMPOTENCY_REF)"

git -C "$IDEMPOTENCY_REPO" checkout -q "$IDEMPOTENCY_REF"
helm upgrade --install idempotency-service "$IDEMPOTENCY_REPO/charts/idempotency-service" \
  -f "$IDEMPOTENCY_REPO/charts/idempotency-service/values-ephemeral.yaml" \
  -f services/idempotency.yaml \
  --namespace "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" --create-namespace

# Dapr S3 binding for blob integrations, pointing at the Garage fixtures
# bucket (blob/ root). Applied here, after the tooling namespace exists.
kubectl apply -f infra/dapr-s3-binding.yaml

log "Installing business-incident-service (ref: $INCIDENT_REF)"

git -C "$INCIDENT_REPO" checkout -q "$INCIDENT_REF"
helm upgrade --install business-incident-service "$INCIDENT_REPO/charts/business-incident-service" \
  -f "$INCIDENT_REPO/charts/business-incident-service/values-ephemeral.yaml" \
  -f services/business-incident.yaml \
  --namespace "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Wait and report
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Waiting for deployments"

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" rollout status deploy/idempotency-service --timeout=300s
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" rollout status deploy/business-incident-service --timeout=300s

# The migration job is not guaranteed to exist the moment helm returns;
# poll for existence before waiting on completion.
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" get job business-incident-service-migrate >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 2
done
kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" get job business-incident-service-migrate >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "migration job never appeared"

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" wait --for=condition=complete job/business-incident-service-migrate --timeout=180s

log "Environment is up"

kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE_SERVICES" get pods
echo
echo "Smoke test:"
echo "  kubectl -n $NAMESPACE_SERVICES port-forward svc/business-incident-service 8080:8080"
echo "  curl localhost:8080/healthz/ready"
echo
echo "RabbitMQ management UI: kubectl -n $NAMESPACE_INFRA port-forward svc/rabbitmq 15672:15672 (guest/guest)"
echo
echo "Garage S3 (fixtures bucket '$GARAGE_BUCKET', roots sftp/ and blob/):"
echo "  endpoint: http://garage.$NAMESPACE_INFRA.svc.cluster.local:3900 (in-cluster)"
echo "  kubectl -n $NAMESPACE_INFRA port-forward svc/garage 3900:3900 (from host)"
echo "  access key: $GARAGE_KEY_ID  secret: $GARAGE_KEY_SECRET"
echo "  region: garage  (use path-style addressing)"
echo "SFTPGo admin UI: kubectl -n $NAMESPACE_INFRA port-forward svc/sftpgo 8080:80 (admin/admin, /web/admin)"
echo "SFTPGo SFTP: kubectl -n $NAMESPACE_INFRA port-forward svc/sftpgo 2022:22 (user sftpgo/sftpgo, chrooted to sftp/)"
echo "Tear down: ./down.sh"

The local render replaces the sentinel with a different convention — see "The
local overlay" below.

## imageNamespace must match CI

Customers disagree on the path segment between the registry and the image name —
one uses the customer slug, another uses `integrations`. The template defaults
to `integrations`. If CI pushes elsewhere, edit the created GitOps source before
merge so the workload and `component.yaml` name the same image repository.

## The local overlay

`overlays/local/` is rendered by `intropy manifests render --env local`: a
one-off render for the local development cluster, piped straight to
`kubectl apply -f -`. It differs from the environment overlays in three ways.

**The image reference is pinned to a bare name.** `deployment.yaml` and
`cronjob-local.yaml` render `image: {{ .name }}` — no registry prefix, no
tag — exactly when `.env` is `local`. `intropy manifests render` writes a root
kustomization whose `images[]` entries rewrite that reference to `<name>:dev`,
the tag the k3s setup scripts build and load component images under. kustomize
matches `images[]` on the exact rendered string and **silently ignores a miss**, so
the bare-name shape is part of the contract; the CLI also fails the render if
any built Deployment image has no tag, as a second net.

**The fixture bindings live here.** `overlays/local/fixtures/` carries one
Dapr binding skeleton per fixture type — the closed catalog declared in
`spec.local.fixtures` (`sftp`, `smb`, `http`, `file`). Each file renders one
`Component` per topology connector whose binding for this local render names
that fixture, and nothing when none do. Repeat
`--binding <connector>=<fixture>` for reproducible renders; an interactive
terminal asks for omitted choices with a Huh selector. Choices are validated
against the catalog and never persisted.

**Dev values, not placeholders.** Every fixture skeleton points at the
conventional fixture server the k3s setup scripts always install —
`sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22` (`intropy`/`intropy`),
`smb.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:445`, `http.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:8080`
(wiremock-style stub), and `/data/<connector>` in the component's own
container for `file`. That fixture contract — namespace, service names,
ports, credentials, the bare image reference above — is shared with the k3s
setup scripts and is the only coupling between the two; the rendered
manifests are otherwise generic and apply to any cluster with Dapr and the
fixtures installed. Local output must apply cleanly on first run, so nothing
under `overlays/local/` renders a `REPLACE-ME-*` value.

The overlay renders no namespace and no image override of its own: the CLI's
root kustomization sets both, so the same overlay serves any `--namespace`
and any `--image` override without re-rendering.

### Why a connector's binding lives with the component

`intropy manifests create` renders bindings on the host because
customer-cluster credentials are environment-owned and shared at the system
level. The local
cluster needs no secret material — fixture credentials are public dev values —
and the catalog files *can* live on the host (they render
identically there). They live here anyway: a connector is scoped to exactly
the app-ids that use it, and keeping the binding beside the block that
resolves it keeps one component's fixture choices out of every other
component's render. The host's `base/bindings/bindings.yaml` is not rendered
locally — the CLI renders only the local overlay, and only this overlay
references fixture files.

### ApplicationSet safety

If this rendered tree ever lands in a GitOps repository, `overlays/local/`
must not produce an ArgoCD Application. It cannot: the ApplicationSet that
fans overlays out to clusters generates from its *cluster* generator, which
matches only clusters registered in ArgoCD — the local development cluster
=====HOST=====
| topology has connectors | `base/bindings/` at all |

`base/kustomization.yaml` references `dapr/pubsub-{{ .pubsub }}.yaml`, so the
list needs no conditional — the file name follows the parameter.

Adding a broker is a new `pubsub-<name>.yaml.tmpl`, a new `enum` value and a new
rule. The CLI is not involved: it passes `platform.pubsub` through from
`deploy.yaml` without knowing what the values mean.

## Shared pub/sub is identical across environments

The pub/sub components live in `base/` and do not vary by environment. What varies
is the *credential*, and a Component reaches that through `secretKeyRef` — so the
same YAML resolves to different values in each environment's namespace. The
overlays are a `namespace:` and a `resources:` line.

One customer repository does vary the broker per overlay (in-memory in dev,
RabbitMQ in prod). That is a deviation, not the convention, and this template
does not reproduce it.

The local cluster is the exception, and it is no variation at all:
`intropy manifests render --env local` always renders with
